lines: Alex Kantrowitz and Ranjan Roy argue Big Tech is facing a market correction as investors stop rewarding heavy AI infrastructure spending and start questioning whether the core businesses can sustain it.

They say the web's old bargain, where search sends traffic to publishers in exchange for crawling rights, is breaking down as AI overviews answer queries directly, while closed-ecosystem ad models like Meta's and Amazon's hold up better than open-web search ads.

On Anthropic's S-1, the hosts see a highly cash-efficient business but suspect its margins are flattered by discounted compute from Amazon and Google, and note the employee equity it creates could concentrate a startling share of top-tier wealth in a few AI firms.
They argue an aggressive LLM price war is commoditizing models, and that better compute efficiency could paradoxically hurt data center operators by shrinking demand for the build-out.
They also worry AI recording wearables could turn everyday conversation into a performance by making every moment replayable.
title: Big Tech's Ugly Week, Getting Rich At Anthropic, AI Costs Plunge
